bc_jericho_wall.blurb: Jericho Wall is the west-facing side of Cave Hill, at the far northern end of the Skaha Bluffs near Penticton. It holds eleven bolted sport lines, and this is a hard-leaning wall: most climbs sit in the 5.12 and 5.13 range, with only a pair of 5.10 and 5.11 routes to warm up on. The wall is steep and the base is open with little tree cover, so it catches the afternoon sun and offers almost no shade. Reaching it takes a longer walk than the popular sectors, and it sees few visitors. Development is still ongoing, so expect a quiet day aimed at strong sport climbers.

bc_valley_of_the_lost_tribe.blurb: A small crag tucked into Murrin Park, just south of Squamish, lying a short distance past its neighbour Commonwealth. The wall leans back rather than standing vertical, which suits the mostly moderate climbing: ten of the eleven routes here are protected with trad gear and one is bolted. Grades run from easy 5.6 up through the 5.9 to 5.10 range, with a couple of harder lines near 5.12. It offers a relaxed alternative for climbers working through moderates, and a rack with doubles in the smaller cams is worth bringing. Reaching it involves a brief gully scramble after following the park's loop trail to Commonwealth.

bc_the_ramparts.blurb: The Ramparts is the first rock you meet when walking the main trail from the lower lot at Skaha Bluffs, forming the entrance to The Fortress sector above Penticton. Eleven routes mix bolted sport lines with gear-protected trad, almost all of them in the 5.10 to 5.12 range, so it suits climbers past the beginner stage rather than those looking for easy ones. Because it sits right beside the car park it is a quick place to start or finish a day, and a good pick when you want short travel time before heading on to the larger walls nearby.

bc_creekside_wall.blurb: Creekside Wall is the first rock face on your right as you descend into Cougar Canyon in Kalamalka Lake Provincial Park, south of Vernon. It is a short wall that is friendly to beginners, with eleven routes: a split between sport and trad, many also easy to set up as top-ropes. Grades start at 5.2 and climb to about 5.10, with most lines in the 5.5 to 5.10 band, so a first-timer and a keen intermediate can share the day. The gneiss here is grainy and textured. You can reach the top via the right-hand trail at the signs, or walk down the left trail through a gully to the base.
